{{Short description|American Professor of Physics}}
'''James Stephen Langer''' is an American professor of physics at the [[University of California at Santa Barbara]].<ref name="langerhomepage">{{Cite web | url=http://www.physics.ucsb.edu/~langer/ | title=Professor James S. Langer, Biosketch | access-date=2010-10-15 | archive-date=2011-07-25 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725093723/http://www.physics.ucsb.edu/~langer/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Born in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]], in 1934, Langer graduated from [[Taylor Allderdice High School]] in 1951.  He attended [[Carnegie Institute of Technology]] and the [[University of Birmingham]], earning a B.A. in physics from the former in 1955 and a Ph.D. in mathematical physics from the latter in 1958.<ref name="aps99">{{Cite web |url=http://www.apscenttalks.org/chair.cfm?sessID=33 |access-date=2010-10-15 }}</ref> A [[Marshall Scholar]] at Birmingham, his thesis advisor was [[Rudolf Peierls]]. After receiving his doctorate, he began his career in the physics department at the Carnegie Institute of Technology (which later became [[Carnegie Mellon University]]), where he would stay until 1982. He then joined UCSB's [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics|Institute for Theoretical Physics]] as professor. Between 1989 and 1995, he served as its director.

According to his profile at UCSB, Langer's research focuses on theories of nonequilibrium phenomena, including the kinetics of [[phase transitions]], [[pattern formation]] in [[crystal growth]], the dynamics of [[earthquakes]], and deformation and failure in noncrystalline solids.<ref name="langerhomepage"/>

Langer served as president of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2000 and as vice president of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] from 2001 to 2005.
He was the founding editor of the ''[[Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics]]'' as of 2010.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-co-1-072910-100001|title=Preface|journal=Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics|year=2010|volume=1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031016-025141|title=My Career as a Theoretical Physicist—So Far|year=2017|last1=Langer|first1=J.S.|journal=Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics|volume=8|pages=1–11|bibcode=2017ARCMP...8....1L|doi-access=free}}</ref>
His awards include the APS's [[Oliver Buckley Prize]] in 1997.
